newsitem.title: USA: N.J. in search of site for nuclear dump - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. in search of site for nuclear dump - paper.

text.p: New Jersey officials are trying to raise $73 million over the next five years as part of plan to convince a town or city to accept a low-level nuclear waste dump, Star-Ledger reported Tuesday.
The money, collected for New Jersey Low-Level Radioactive Waste Disposal Facility Siting Board, would be funded by fees on utilities, hospitals and other generators of radioactive waste.
If a town accepts the dump, which the paper said appeared unlikely, it would receive about $2 million annually from the state.
Under a 1980 law passed by Congress, every state must develop plans to handle their own waste, rather than send it to disposal facilities out of state, according to the paper.
